code_b_label: deal.II (build and run the C++ program)
interface: the line x = 5/8, where the two materials meet
coefficients: subdomain A: lambda = 577, mu = 385 (E = 962885/962, nu = 577/1924); subdomain B: lambda = 577, mu = 1155 (E = 4667355/1732, nu = 577/3464). The shear modulus jumps by a factor 3 across the interface; lambda is the same on both sides.
interface_condition: the displacement vector and the traction sigma.n (BOTH components)
element: vector Lagrange P1 elements in both codes
mesh_text: uniform meshes, h halved per level: h = 1/8, 1/16, 1/32
bc_text: u = 0 (both components) on the entire outer boundary
iface_header: x, y, ux, uy, tx, ty
probe_iface: the 44 points (x, y) = (5/8, 1/4 + (i+0.5)*1/2/44) for i = 0, 1, ..., 43. These cover the INTERIOR of the interface only: the two points where the interface meets the outer boundary are corners of the split problem and the recovered flux there does not converge, so they are not graded
iface_clearance_reason: the interface ends are Dirichlet-Neumann corners of the split problem and carry a stress singularity the monolithic problem does not have; the exported traction there gets WORSE under refinement (measured 2.11x -> 2.51x the true value over a 4x refinement), so grading them would fail a correct submission
notes_public: the normal and shear interface stiffness ratios of this material pair differ by an order of magnitude (both follow from the Lame parameters and subdomain widths above). A single scalar relaxation factor chosen for one component can diverge in the other; a componentwise or worst-component choice is safer.
evidence_grade_reason: exact manufactured solution: proves the answer is CORRECT
qoi: convergence order of the coupled displacement, plus the two-sided interface traction jump
graded_against: hidden manufactured solution (true error) AND reference-free mesh halving
